what: What one accumulation step costs, split into the half an on-screen accumulation would pay and the half only the offline film pays. Plan-of-record A-3, for Visual-Marketing plan §3.2 M-6.
why: M-6 deferred pending measurement, arguing the repo's only figure (103.8 ms/frame) 'includes readback and PNG encode the on-screen path does not pay'. That is true and it is the wrong way round: the scope step is the LARGER half.
harness: SemanticMapFrameSequence, instrumented at A-3 with a scopeMilliseconds split. TEST_RUNNER_RENDER_MAP_FRAMES_DIR=<dir> xcodebuild test -only-testing FRUSExplorerTests/SemanticMapFrameSequenceTests, iPhone 17 simulator, erased first.
findings: The scope step is 57-58% of the frame, not a remainder. Stripping the offline-only stages leaves the larger half.
Per-step cost GROWS with the accumulated scope: 44 ms at the first decile, 93 ms at the last. It is a fixed whole-corpus mask rebuild PLUS a marking pass over the cumulative union.
44-93 ms of MAIN-ACTOR CPU per step against a 16.7 ms frame budget at 60fps: three to six frame budgets blocked per step.
The absolute total (129-132 ms) runs ~24% above the runbook's 104.9 ms on the same device class, reproducibly across two runs. The SHARE is the robust finding; the absolute is this machine's.

decadeProjection.note: A decade run is 17 steps. A step's cost is set by the cumulative scope it rebuilds, so each decade step costs what the volume-grain step at the same cumulative document count cost. These are measured values at those points, not extrapolations.

verdict: M-6 is NOT viable as designed. Seventeen steps of 44-93 ms main-actor CPU is 17 visible hitches, not an animation. It becomes viable only if the step is made incremental: accumulation is MONOTONIC, so a step need only mark the newly added volumes' rows and increment regionCounts for those - O(added) rather than O(corpus). SemanticMapColouring.scopeMask rebuilds from scratch because it is general over any scope set; an accumulation-specific path would not have to.
